subject: Renewal activation playbook, staged discount triggers & invoice timing
messages:
From: Sanjay Rao <sanjay@acme.io>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-28T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Renewal + capacity uplift — pricing conversation

Hi Laura,

We're kicking off our renewal discussion for Acme's deployment (term ends 2027-06-30). Usage has been ahead of our initial forecast — we need to add ~40% capacity for the next 12 months and lock pricing for at least the first 9 months of the renewal while we complete our cost model.

High level ask: can Redwood provide a staged discount tied to committed throughput (so we have predictability), a one-time onboarding credit to offset the migration/config work, and a short-term price hold (9 months) on the active model family? Procurement (cc'd: Emily Park) will need invoice timing and PO requirements.

Before we loop legal/procurement formally, wanted to understand what flexibility you have on discounts and credits — also any operational requirements from your side for a 40% capacity uplift.

Thanks,
Sanjay Rao
Head of ML Infrastructure
Acme Corp

---
Acme internal contact for procurement: Emily Park (epark@acme.io)
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Sanjay Rao <sanjay@acme.io>
Cc: Emily Park <epark@acme.io>
Date: 2027-04-29T11:05:18-07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal + capacity uplift — pricing conversation

Hi Sanjay — appreciate the heads-up.

We can structure a renewal that balances predictability for Acme and a realistic uplift for Redwood. Draft proposal below (high level):

- Commitment and staged discount:
  - Commit floor: 100M tokens/month baseline (matches current committed throughput).
  - Tier 1 (1.0–1.99x baseline): 10% discount on per-token invoice rate.
  - Tier 2 (2.0–2.99x baseline): 15% discount on per-token invoice rate.
  - Tier 3 (>=3.0x baseline): accelerate review for a custom rate (requires 60-day notice).
- Price hold: lock the per-token rate for 9 months from the effective renewal date for the referenced model family.
- One-time onboarding credit: $15,000 applied against the first invoice to cover migration/configuration.
- SLA / reliability commitment: 99.9% availability target. If we miss the SLO in a quarter, customer is eligible for a 5% credit on that quarter's invoice (capped at 1 quarter).
- Operational: 30-day ramp window for the 40% capacity uplift; we will provide a migration checklist and a short observability runbook.
- Legal / procurement asks: we will provide an updated SOW and DocuSign bundle once commercial terms are agreed. We need a PO or signed DocuSign by 2027-05-10 to guarantee the proposed discounts.

Attachments: redwood_proposal_acme_v3.pdf (proposal), SOW-Acme-2027.docx (SOW draft). DocuSign: https://www.docusign.com/TP/SigningStart?env=prod&doc=ACME-SOW-2027

If that high-level looks good, Emily — please confirm invoice routing and PO timing. Sanjay — would you prefer the onboarding credit applied up front or spread across the first two invoices?

Thanks,
Laura Bennett
Account Executive — Enterprise
Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0167
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>

Date: 2027-04-29T11:12:05-07:00

Jonas / Grace — forwarding SANJAY's note and my proposed commercial outline above. Two quick asks:

1) Onboarding credit: I put $15k in the draft to reduce friction for migration. Can we cap this at $10k and treat the remainder as an onboarding service add-on billable to us if they request extra deliverables?
2) Ramp: Acme is asking for 40% immediate capacity. Ops prefers a 30-day ramp with a 20% burst buffer in month one. Can we confirm we have the burst headroom without impacting other Dedicated customers?

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-30T08:38:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Renewal + capacity uplift — pricing conversation (need approval on credits / ramp)

Laura — thanks for the summary. I support the staged discount approach, but recommend the following adjustments before we send the final SOW:

- Reduce the onboarding credit to $10,000 (apply to invoice 1). We can offer a one-time up-sellable services package if they want managed migration beyond what's in the SOW.
- Approve the 30-day ramp with a 20% burst allowance in month 1. Make the additional burst conditional and time-limited (30 days).
- Add a commit floor clause: if average monthly usage falls below 0.8x baseline over the first 3 months, standard overage/proration applies and discount tiers are re-evaluated.
- Legal note: require a standard termination-for-convenience notice (60 days) with pro-rated true-up on committed tokens.

Once legal signs off on the termination/true-up language, we can send the DocuSign package to Acme.

— Jonas
Head of Sales — Enterprise
jonas.weber@redwood.com

Date: 2027-05-05T15:42:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal + capacity uplift — pricing conversation

Hi Laura — thanks for the clear proposal and for accommodating Acme's timing. Procurement is ok with the commercial outline with two small asks before we sign:

1) Net payment terms: our AP requires Net 45 rather than Net 30. Can Redwood accept Net 45 for this renewal?
2) Invoice routing: please send all invoices and the final signed SOW to invoice@acme.io and include PO number PO-9853 on the invoice. Our internal PO will be issued after DocuSign is complete but please include the PO field so AP can match.

We accept the $10k onboarding credit and the staged discount tiers. For the burst capacity in month one, we'd like that represented as a 20% temporary allowance (no additional charge during a 30-day window). After that window, usage will bill against the applicable tier.

Please send the DocuSign link and final SOW with the invoice routing/PO fields included. If we can get DocuSign executed by 2027-05-10 we'll proceed with the renewal on the terms above.

Thanks — Emily
